scope: Isolated Castle Game Engine WebGL matrix and numeric-list conversion candidate: contiguous-layout checks, signed-byte bounds, owned bulk copies, reproducible baseline/candidate Pascal transfer tests and correctly bound candidate application staging. Application dependency adoption and existing buffer-upload helpers are outside this development-candidate scope.

intuitiveness.evidence: The transfer README and wrapper provide explicit baseline/candidate modes, diagnostics, hash metadata and a required signed-range switch. The current URL-mode result is clearly reported as 9493 legacy plus 13 signed-boundary checks.

accuracy.evidence: The fresh URL-mode result passes 9506 checks with no errors, including all 13 boundary assertions, and reports 2000 matrix conversions. The candidate source has contiguous-layout guards, QWord byte arithmetic, High(LongInt) rejection and owned copies. The URL-mode verification has null engine/WASM hashes, and the full application wrapper plus baseline/scene comparison is still pending.

wowFactor.evidence: For this developer-tooling scope, the fresh boundary result and 12 ms diagnostic conversion run are useful evidence. A controlled current baseline comparison and final application scene evidence are still absent, so no stronger grade is warranted.

thinkingOutOfTheBox.evidence: Synthetic logical list counts exercise the signed 2 GiB rejection path without allocating the enormous arrays, while the same probe checks exact scalar bits, ownership and memory growth. This preserves the public conversion API and leaves dependency adoption separate.

blockingFindings: Complete and retain the full wrapper run with candidate source and generated WASM hashes, then run the matching pinned baseline with the same probe and toolchain.
Bind current application scene/style/recovery evidence to the frozen WASM, data, host, manifest and runtime-part hashes; the transfer URL result alone does not establish application behavior.
Keep the candidate pending and do not treat it as an adopted Castle dependency or as approval of terrain, renderer, style or recovery features.
